caption:
Every week, BestMediaInfo's Talent Tracker publishes another round of leadership moves. Somewhere in that list is your new boss, or your boss's new boss.

Here is what nobody tells you: a new leader resets every reputation in the building to zero. Your eight years of delivery aren't in the room. Your reputation with the last regime doesn't travel. Only the first three interactions count, and they're being graded whether you know it or not.

In command, a change of leadership meant the same thing. You were assessed fresh. Bearing before briefing. How you stood, how you spoke, what you didn't say.

So decide now. In your first meeting with the new leadership, what does your posture say before you open your mouth? Does your voice drop at the end of a sentence or climb? Do you fill silence or hold it?

The track record gets you into the room. Presence decides what happens there.

topic.title: Weekly CXO churn means someone just got a new boss
topic.angle: A new leader resets every reputation in the building to zero — eight years of track record aren't in the room, only the first three interactions are, which is precisely where command presence decides outcomes.
topic.why_now: BestMediaInfo's Talent Tracker publishes weekly (latest edition ~13 days old), giving a genuinely renewable live peg as reorgs and new skip-levels cascade down two and three layers.

rationale: A stark, text-only visual matches the no-nonsense command tone and keeps the single hard idea — reputation resets to zero — front and centre without decorative distraction.
